assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology to incretin-based therapies is a rare complete arc: gut-hormone biology, receptor pharmacology, and drugs (semaglutide, tirzepatide-class) that have transformed diabetes and now obesity care, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality is clear and the societal impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology and clinical biology of GLP-1, Drucker the intestinotrophic and receptor biology and the translational bridge, Mojsov the identification of the bioactive truncated peptide. Knudsen's medicinal chemistry was decisive for the drug but is industrial development; a three-person prize is plausible but who to omit (Habener is not on the list; Mojsov's priority is contested) is a real question.
assessment.maturity: Mature and strongly confirmed by large independent outcome trials. Timing is arguably pressing given the scale of clinical impact.
uncertainties: Credit split between basic discovery (Mojsov, Habener, Holst) and drug development (Knudsen) is unresolved.
Mojsov's priority versus Habener's group is disputed; I rely on recall, not verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality (living drugs). Concept, proof of principle and clinical translation are all clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed the foundational costimulatory CAR design, June the first successful clinical translation (CD19 CAR-T in CLL) and Rosenberg the adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Eshhar and others are not in the credited set. The trio is reasonable but the exact weighting is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and multi-year remission data confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers. Solid-tumour success and safety (cytokine release, secondary malignancy) remain open, but recognition for the proven part is timely.
uncertainties: Omission of Zelig Eshhar from the supplied credit may weaken a fair allocation.
Rosenberg's contribution is adoptive cell therapy broadly, not strictly CAR design.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling and a general principle of proteostasis. It is conceptually original, mechanistically complete (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6, PERK) and relevant to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter's and Mori's groups independently defined the pathway; Ire1 kinase/RNase and unconventional splicing of HAC1 mRNA (Walter, Mori and Sidrauski) are the decisive steps. The two-person configuration is clean and well supported.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation; the pathway is textbook. Therapeutic exploitation is still emerging, but the discovery is fully mature.
uncertainties: Physiology-or-medicine fit rests on disease relevance rather than a direct therapy.
Contributions of others (e.g. Ron, Harding, Haze) fall outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR is the central integrator of nutrient and growth signalling, with consequences for metabolism, ageing, cancer, immunity and transplantation (rapamycin). Impact is broad and long-lasting.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified the TOR genes and the biology of TOR signalling; Schreiber's work on the FKBP12-rapamycin complex and the mTOR target protein was decisive for the mechanism. Sabatini contributed key mTORC1 pathway components and regulation but has an unsettled public standing; I leave him out and note that Brown, Sabatini and others also contributed to mTOR protein identification.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and heavily confirmed, with clinical drug use (rapalogs) established. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Attribution for mTOR protein identification is shared among several groups.
Exclusion of Sabatini is a judgment on credit allocation and not on science alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS, cGAMP and STING defined a major innate-immune pathway central to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and anti-tumour immunity, a clear conceptual advance.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING as the adaptor. Ishikawa shares the STING discovery with Barber, and Sun and Wu worked in Chen's group. Two laureates is the fairest configuration; Ishikawa's role is a real allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed with a rapidly expanding literature. Therapeutic agonist and antagonist programmes are early and have not yet delivered approved drugs, so clinical maturity is incomplete.
uncertainties: Ishikawa's credit alongside Barber is unresolved.
Clinical translation is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-lived, self-organizing epithelial organoids from single Lgr5 adult stem cells opened a new platform for modelling disease, drug testing and personalised medicine. It is original and widely adopted across fields.
assessment.attribution: Clevers identified Lgr5 stem cells and led the organoid derivation; Sato performed the key culture work as first author of the 2009 paper. A two-person prize is clean, though the stem-cell identity work and the culture method could be viewed as separate parts.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed and widely used. Clinical impact is still emerging and the prize case rests more on enabling technology than on proven therapeutic outcome, so some may see timing as early.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is a technology or a discovery is debatable.
Overlap with earlier 3D culture and stem-cell work by others is not captured in the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of targeted kinase inhibition. Impact on oncology is foundational.
assessment.attribution: Lydon built the compound programme, Druker led clinical translation and demonstrated activity in CML, and Sawyers defined resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors. The trio is coherent, though Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford and the BCR-ABL discovery were earlier work outside this credit.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with over two decades of survival data and independent confirmation. If it were to be recognised, the main concern is that the field has long been waiting, rather than prematurity.
uncertainties: Prior discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL sits outside the supplied credit.
Industrial versus academic contribution is a weighing question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, with striking motor-function benefit in infants. It validated splice-switching oligonucleotides as a therapeutic class.
assessment.attribution: Krainer identified the splicing regulatory elements and ISS-N1 target; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and development with Ionis. The pairing fits the mechanism-to-drug arc. Others, including Hua and Singh, and other antisense pioneers contributed.
assessment.maturity: Approved and confirmed over several years of follow-up; the modality is now extended to other diseases. Possibly somewhat early as a general antisense recognition, but credible.
uncertainties: Contributions of other splicing and antisense researchers may complicate a prize.
Long-term outcomes in treated patients are still accumulating.
